resolutions.researcher_notes: Original current_ref (almasryalyoum.com/news/details/103848) is dead (DEAD_LINK per brief) and was gem.wiki-sourced Arabic press anyway, so not re-cited. This segment (Abu Qurqas-Asyut) is 'stage 3' of the wider Cairo-Aswan South Valley/Upper Egypt Gas Pipeline. The Australian Pipeliner (2009-09-23, staff writer) reports Petrojet had 'most recently completed stages three and four' (stage 3 = 136km, 32in, Minya governorate/Abu Qurqas to Assiut). Petroleum Africa (2011-01-03) reports Mubarak's Dec-2010 inauguration of the full pipeline in Aswan, explicitly listing 'stage three extends 136 km from the governorate of Minya to Assiut' among the completed stages that make up the now-operating grid connection to Aswan. Two independent trade outlets (different publishers/dates, Australian vs African/Egyptian trade press, tracing to different press events - 2009 progress report vs 2011 inauguration wrap) both confirm this stage was built and forms part of the operating pipeline; status 'operating' is well supported by context (construction completion + inauguration + ongoing grid service) even though neither uses the literal word 'operating'. No contradiction found on status.

Could not corroborate the recorded LengthKnown=147.00 km for the Abu Qurqas-Asyut segment. Every independent source found gives a materially different figure: EIB financing summary sheet (eib.org/en/projects/all/20060137, project promoter GASCO, EUR 50m signed 2006-12-21) states 'a 120km long high-pressure gas pipeline section between Abu Qurqas, next to the city of Al Minya, and Asyut.' Three separate trade-press sources instead converge on 136 km: Oil & Gas Journal (2008-01-28, ogj.com/.../17217939) describes the Abu Qorqas-to-Asyut phase as '136 km (85 miles)' of 32-inch pipe at an estimated LE520 million; MEED (meed.com/gasco-pipeline-on-course/, reporting Nov-2006 design phase) gives 'Abu Qurqas to Assiut... 136 kilometers' at $75 million via Petrojet/Enppi; The Australian Pipeliner (2009-09-23) likewise reports 'Stage three saw 136 km of 32 inch diameter pipeline laid from the governorate of Minya to Assiut.' None of the four independent sources (EIB, OGJ, MEED, Pipeliner) supports the GEM-recorded 147.00 km value - candidates cluster at 120 km (EIB, narrower engineered section) or 136 km (OGJ+MEED+Pipeliner, 3 independent, same 32in/Petrojet/Enppi project). Flagging as a value discrepancy for Update review rather than fabricating support for 147.00; closest well-corroborated alternative is 136 km. Not proposing a ref since no source actually supports the stated value (per no-orphan/no-fabricated-support rule).

Start=Abu Qurqas (Minya, Egypt), End=Asyut (Asyut, Egypt) are directly and identically confirmed by two independent sources: the EIB project summary sheet (financing institution, project promoter GASCO) states the section runs 'between Abu Qurqas, next to the city of Al Minya, and Asyut'; Oil & Gas Journal's 2008 feature independently describes 'the second phase' of the South Valley pipeline running from Abu Qorqas to Asyut (following the Beni Suef-Abu Qorqas first phase completed mid-2007). MEED's 2006 report corroborates the same Abu Qurqas-to-Assiut routing (not cited to avoid redundancy beyond the 2-source requirement, but consistent). No contradiction on endpoints/governorates - both StartState/Province=Minya and EndState/Province=Asyut match the sourced description exactly.
